newsitem.title: USA: Crews extinguish fire, work to cap U.S. Gulf well.
newsitem.headline: Crews extinguish fire, work to cap U.S. Gulf well.

text.p: Crews extinguished flames but continued working to cap a natural gas well that burned out of control for two days after a blowout on an American Exploration Co platform in the Gulf of Mexico, officials said on Friday.
A plume of natural gas from the subsea well was still shooting uncontrolled into the sky, raising concern of a possible explosion and fire if the gas stream is reignited accidentally, officials said.
"Until the well has been successfully capped, the possibility of renewed fire exists due to leaking natural gas," the Coast Guard and well operator American Exploration said in a joint statement.

The fire had been burning since Tuesday, when it ignited while crews were removing safety equipment from the shut-in well on an American Exploration platform about 100 miles off the coast of Louisiana in East Cameron Block 328.

An oil sheen tied to the blowout had dissipated by Thursday and little environmental damage was expected as the natural gas vented into the sky, officials said. But skimmer boats remained nearby in the event of an oil spill, they said.
The fire was put out late Thursday by crews spraying the platform with water cannons from an offshore supply ship and a barge, the Coast Guard and a company spokesman said.
The company had expected the fire to burn for up to two weeks, and plans to drill a relief well to intercept and cut off the flow of gas from the well.

A cluster of wells feeding into the platform had been producing 7.2 million cubic feet per day of natural gas and 300 barrels per day of oil, or less than 10 percent of the Houston-based company's gas and oil production.
